newsitem.title: USA: Bill will tie U.S. aid to Bosnia arrests.
newsitem.headline: Bill will tie U.S. aid to Bosnia arrests.

text.p: Two senators introduced legislation on Wednesday that would cut U.S. reconstruction aid to Bosnia if authorities there do not turn war criminals over to a special Hague tribunal for prosecution.

"The simple fact is that neither the Serb authorities within Bosnia and Herzegovina nor the Croat authorities in the (Croat-Bosnia) federation are meeting their obligations to hand over the indicted war criminals," Sen. Dianne Feinstein said.

The California Democrat and Sen. Frank Lautenberg, a New Jersey Democrat, introduced a bill that would reduce the $5.1 billion U.S. contribution to the international reconstruction programme in Bosnia if war criminals are not arrested and turned over to the U.N. tribunal for former Yugoslavia.
"Reconstruction without reconciliation will not be effective in the long run, and the apprehension of war criminals is essential for reconciliation to take place," Lautenberg said.
He said U.S. contributions for economic aid for large municipal projects would be cut off but humanitarian and democratization aid, for housing and elections for example, would not.

The bill would prohibit U.S. aid to any project in which an indicted war criminal is involved and aid to communities that harbour war criminals would be limited to funds for emergency food and medicine, and removal of land mines.
